label: Pepwave MAX HD4 quad-LTE mobile router
description: Peplink Pepwave MAX HD4 - rugged vehicle router with four embedded LTE modems and four redundant SIM slots for SpeedFusion bandwidth bonding, two 100/1000 Ethernet WAN ports, eight 100/1000 Ethernet LAN ports (802.3at PoE output available via the PoE kit), USB WAN, dual-band Wi-Fi AP and Wi-Fi WAN. 12-56 V DC terminal block, GPS, -40 to 65 C class rugged certification (EN 50155 railway, EN 61373 shock/vibration).
notes: The datasheet labels the copper directly: '**2x 100/1000M Ethernet WAN**' and '**8x 100/1000M Ethernet LAN**', so 2+8 is quoted, not inferred - and note the LAN ports are 100/1000, not 10/100/1000. **Four** embedded modems with four redundant SIM slots is the opposite of the BR1 Pro's single modem: this box really does bond four cellular links, so there are four `wwan` bearers and a lab can demonstrate SpeedFusion bonding with four different carriers. The 8 LAN ports are marked '**802.3at PoE Output #**' with a footnote '#PoE Kit is available Separately', and Peplink publishes **no aggregate PoE budget** - so no `poeOut` is declared. Crediting eight ports at 30 W would invent a 240 W supply the vendor never states; a lab that needs powered ports should treat them as plain copper until the kit is fitted. A WAN activation licence can convert LAN ports 1-3 into WAN ports 3-5, which is a licence, not a different chassis.
